LESSON: GRAMMAR IN USE 9.3.1 CONJUNCTIONS: CORRELATIVE CONJUNCTIONS

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade 9
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 9
Topic 9.3: Grammar In Use 9.3.1 Conjunctions: Correlative Conjunctions
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Grammar In Use 9.3.1 Conjunctions: Correlative Conjunctions, part of Strand 9 in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade 9 ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: How do we join sentences?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify the elements of a narrative composition,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Grammar In Use 9.3.1 Conjunctions: Correlative Conjunctions in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. articulate signs of the elements of a narrative composition,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Grammar In Use 9.3.1 Conjunctions: Correlative Conjunctions in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. uses the elements of a narrative composition in a story,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Grammar In Use 9.3.1 Conjunctions: Correlative Conjunctions in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. appreciate the role of background information in the creation of credible stories. • Individually, learner is guided to sign read or read samples of narrative compositions from text books. • Individually, learner is guided to identify and sign the introduction, body and conclusion of a sample composition. • Individually, learner is guided to brainstorm possible topics for narrative compositions. • Individually, learner is guided to tell or sign a story from their own experiences. • Individually, learner is guided to plan a narrative composition. • Individually, learner is guided to write a narrative composition. • Individually, learner is guided to edit the composition, • revise the narrative composition. • Individually, learner is guided to read one another’s composition and obtain feedback from peers. • Individually, learner is guided to make corrections to the narrative. • How should we organise our compositi ons? 121 • Individually, learner is guided to display the compositions in a gallery walk, class noticeboard or through social media.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Grammar In Use 9.3.1 Conjunctions: Correlative Conjunctions together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Self-efficacy : Learner embraces teamwork as he/she practises using conjunctions through role playing with peers.

• Communication: Learner develop writing skills as he/she uses conjunctions correctly in written communication.

Values:
Respect is: inculcated as the learner participates in group tasks.

Link to other subjects

The learner is able to relate the concept of conjunctions learnt in English to similar concept in Kiswahili.
